scenarios.label: ROOT/receiver AAA. Declared synthetic pool AAA, BBB, CCC. States A1, B1, C1 each have positive population, matching owner/controller, no cooldown, no lost-local-control, and no reservation. Other-provider markers are false. Country/state bindings are descriptive until the connected adapter accepts typed scopes.

ROOT/receiver AAA is ineligible and has no eligible positive-population owned-and-controlled state. The declared synthetic candidate pool is BBB and CCC, each with one valid matching-owner/controller state and no cooldown or provider markers. Scope bindings are descriptive pending adapter support.

ROOT/receiver AAA controls B_OCCUPIED, owned by BBB. BBB also owns B_HOME controlled by BBB. Both states have positive population; the rest of the declared pool is invalid. This isolates candidate-country eligibility from selected-state validity. Owner/controller bindings are descriptive pending adapter support.

Candidate BBB owns an active Event 31 package across two active states and has one other provider. The existing-provider entry sets individual_crisis_exclude_random_terror=1, excluding its own single boolean provider contribution once. Active Event 31 states do not multiply that marker. Other-provider binding is unresolved.

Conservative frame/lifetime model, not a flat shared temporary-variable dictionary. Compare unallocated adjusted-weight, active-load, pool-array, and resolved-evolution outputs with caller-owned initialized outputs. No temporary-return persistence is assumed.

Bounded source-contract case: caller initializes adjusted weight, active load, and resolved evolution to zero, and creates then clears its own pool array before nested calls. This describes the proposed safe call frame, not current implementation or runtime proof.

Paired candidates AAA and BBB are identical in sites, ownership/control, population, cooldown, reservation, route, all fourteen provider results, and base weight. Only religion, ethnicity, nationality, refugee status, and ordinary ideology vary. Typed pair bindings remain unresolved.

Paired candidates AAA and BBB have identical provider and site eligibility; each site has positive population, but population and demographic cohort sizes differ. Base weight is one in source. Typed state/cohort bindings remain unresolved.

Synthetic candidates: AAA has zero-population state; BBB has future cooldown; CCC has lost local control; DDD is reserved; EEE is special/nonhuman or route-incompatible; FFF has one valid positive-population owned-and-controlled site. Rejection causes are separate; full world candidate enumeration is unresolved.

One root event requests three attempts but only BBB and CCC are declared valid and site-capable; AAA and DDD are invalid. Successes cannot exceed available valid sites. A failed site selection must not count or retain a reservation.

One entry-root event firing, three attempts, and exactly three valid candidates AAA/BBB/CCC. Eligibility is rebuilt per attempt; source reservation is two days. No repeated cadence, seed, recovery distribution, reset, or terminal sequence is asserted. Sequence evidence is withheld until the live pool manifest and cadence inputs are complete.

Global Jihad scenario host RRR differs from candidates AAA/BBB/CCC. Target seeding, extra-state selection, and actor-parent selection are separate callers with their own scenario flags and host scope. This case checks shared-helper caller boundaries only and authorizes no scenario or country-content redesign.
